question.text: 'Unified Structure' is a common cross-border AIF setup. Which of the following BEST describes the Unified Structure?

answer.text: Two separate pooling vehicles, one domestic and one offshore, each directly investing in Indian investee companies
Only offshore pooling, with no Indian AIF registered
A single onshore (Indian) AIF pools commitments from both domestic and offshore investors, with FPIs investing via automatic route
Offshore investors invest directly into investee companies, bypassing the AIF entirely

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.5.2: Unified Structure pools BOTH domestic and offshore commitments into one domestic (Indian) AIF. FPIs invest under automatic route; no Ministry of Finance / RBI approval needed. The Trap: Option A describes Parallel Structure. Option B describes Pure Offshore. Option D describes direct FDI, not Unified. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C is the primary exam for distinguishing Unified vs Parallel vs Feeder vs Pure Offshore. Table 8.1 summarises. Manager's Pro-Tip: Unified is operationally simplest (one fee-earning vehicle) but exposes FPIs to Indian tax. If your anchor FPI is DTAA-sensitive, a master-feeder or parallel may net better after-tax returns.
